classification.difficultyReason: Read the number of x-intercepts and apply the taught correspondence between that count and the sign of the discriminant.

content.prompt: For each of the quadratic functions below, state the sign of the discriminant.

spec.description: Upward parabola with minimum above the horizontal axis and to the right of the vertical axis.
spec.mathematics: Vertical intercept 3, no horizontal intersections. Unlabelled coordinates are schematic.

answer.worked: The graph stays above the $x$-axis, so it has no real roots and $\Delta<0$.

spec.description: Upward parabola tangent to the horizontal axis.

answer.worked: The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=2$, so there is one distinct real root and $\Delta=0$.

spec.description: Upward parabola crossing the horizontal axis twice.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal intercepts −2 and 0, with the minimum below the axis between them. Unlabelled heights are schematic.

answer.worked: The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-2$ and $x=0$, so it has two distinct real roots and $\Delta>0$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with maximum above the horizontal axis and left of the vertical axis.

answer.worked: The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-4$ and $x=1$, so it has two distinct real roots and $\Delta>0$.

spec.description: Downward parabola tangent to the horizontal axis.

answer.worked: The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=1$, so there is one distinct real root and $\Delta=0$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with maximum above the horizontal axis and to the right of the vertical axis.

answer.worked: The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-1$ and $x=3$, so it has two distinct real roots and $\Delta>0$.
